Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact motor vehicle collision at an intersection,
complaining of neck and low back pain with associated stiffness and muscle tension.
The reported mechanism and force of the collision are consistent with the soft tissue
injuries described. No prior injury to the cervical or lumbar regions is known from
history or records. Eighteen visits were completed over the course of care, which is
somewhat longer than typically expected for uncomplicated cervical and lumbar strain,
and treatment included manual therapy, targeted exercise, and modalities for symptom
control. Cervical and lumbar imaging showed no acute fracture, malalignment, or
structural abnormality, and neurological and orthopedic examination findings were
within normal limits. Diagnoses are based largely on the patient's self-reported pain
and funcitonal limitations, as objective findings were limited. Billed services
reflect the treatment rendered, with no duplicate charges identified. Patient is
advised to continue home exercise and to return if symptoms worsen or fail to improve
with ongoing self-management.
